paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. God's judgments are just and true, and the singers say so before a single bowl is poured. They sing, "Great and wonderful are Your works, O Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the nations!" (Revelation 15:3). Later the angel of the waters and the altar say it too (Revelation 16:5-7).

Now look at the people on the receiving end. I think this part is heavy, friend, with the sores, the blood, the scorching heat and the darkness. And through it all, three times they curse God (Revelation 16:9, 11, 21). Twice the passage says they "did not repent" (Revelation 16:9, 11).

So where does that leave you and me? Right in the middle of the bowls, the passage says, "Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed, so that he will not go naked and let his shame be exposed." (Revelation 16:15). I think awake and clothed means being ready before it happens, since a thief sends no calendar invite, and Jesus tells His followers to keep watch because they do not know the day (Matthew 24:42). That's why my ovens stay warm and my cookie boxes keep filling, since I never guess the day and only the Father knows it (Matthew 24:36), and I think you stay ready by keeping watch and growing in the Word, friend, because the bride "has made herself ready" (Revelation 19:7).

problems.problem: The quote "Therefore keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord will come." isn't the BSB's exact words.
The paragraph still does not explain what staying awake and clothed means or how to prepare for Christ’s coming. The oven and cookie-box metaphor remains unexplained.
